hints: Use the relation between power, driving force, and speed ($P = D \times v$) to calculate the forward driving force $D$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $D - R = ma$.
Substitute mass $m = 90\text{ kg}$, acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and the driving force to solve for the resistance force $R$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force from the power output $P = 250\text{ W}$ at speed $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{250}{5} = 50\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the level road with mass $m = 90\text{ kg}$ and acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$D - R = ma \implies 50 - R = 90 \times 0.1 = 9$$
$$R = 50 - 9 = 41\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall the fundamental relation between mechanical power $P$, driving force $D$, and instantaneous speed $v$:
$$P = D \times v \implies D = \frac{P}{v}$$

Substitute the given power $P = 250\text{ W}$ and speed $v = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$D = \frac{250}{5} = 50\text{ N}$$

Set up Newton's second law in the horizontal direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies D - R = ma$$

Substitute $D = 50\text{ N}$, total mass $m = 90\text{ kg}$, and acceleration $a = 0.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$50 - R = 90 \times 0.1$$
$$50 - R = 9$$

Subtract $9$ and add $R$ to both sides:
$$R = 50 - 9 = 41\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Calculates $D = 250/5 = 50\text{ N}$, forms $50 - R = 90(0.1)$, and evaluates $R = 41\text{ N}$.

hints: For steady speed riding uphill, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the driving force balances the sum of the resistance force and the component of weight down the slope.
Set up the equilibrium equation along the incline: $\frac{P}{v} - R - mg \sin 2^\circ = 0$.
Substitute $P = 250\text{ W}$, $R = 41\text{ N}$, $m = 90\text{ kg}$, and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to evaluate the steady speed $v$.
walkthrough:
At a steady speed up the incline, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances resistance and the parallel component of weight:
$$\frac{P}{v} - R - mg \sin 2^\circ = 0$$

Solve for the steady speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{250}{72.408} \approx 3.45\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
When the cyclist moves at a steady speed up a hill inclined at $2^\circ$, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $D$ must equal the total opposing forces along the incline:
$$D = R + mg \sin 2^\circ$$

Express the driving force in terms of the constant power $P = 250\text{ W}$ and steady speed $v$:
$$D = \frac{250}{v}$$

Calculate the parallel component of weight for total mass $m = 90\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$W_{\parallel} = mg \sin 2^\circ = 90 \times 10 \times \sin 2^\circ = 900 \times 0.0348995 \approx 31.4095\text{ N}$$

Add the unchanged resistance force $R = 41\text{ N}$:
$$D = 41 + 31.4095 = 72.4095\text{ N}$$

Equate to $\frac{250}{v}$ and solve for $v$:
$$\frac{250}{v} = 72.4095$$
$$v = \frac{250}{72.4095} \approx 3.4526\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 3.45\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Sets up $250/v - 41 - 900\sin 2^\circ = 0$ and evaluates $v = 3.45\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
